ŋprod¯ductumThis word is a very interesting use case for the encoding of abbreviations. The macron that crosses the long ascending trait of the "d" might well be interpreted as spanning not only over the "d", but also over the first grapheme. The latter, however, already is an abbreviation, since it is a "ŋ" brevigraph normally meaning "prae" (which, through monophthongation, becomes "pre").  So the first grapheme would be involved in two different abbreviations: it is a brevigraph per se, but it is also part of the abbreviation involving the whole word (marked by the macron above it).  However, in my JavaScript code handling the XML/TEI code, I did not think of handling a case in which an "abbr" element is child of another "abbr" element. Also, the macron is mostly over the "d", so I am encoding this as though the macron was over the "d" only.
